tasks.title: Five corpus files share one unread player build and so do not convert
tasks.verify: Measured at v0.5.438: **Go_Go_Dash, Lion_Heart, Pacific_Coast, Radio_ACE and Sun_Never_Shines all share the stored-wave key `cell=$1A43 / store=$104B`**, with Lakers_vs_Celtics one cell away at `$1A6B / $104B`. All six carry this engine's `BD ?? ?? 3D ?? ?? 99 04 D4` idiom -- positive evidence they ARE the family -- yet every one refuses with `UnsupportedSidError: NO HUBBARD PLAYER DETECTED`. By this repo's own rule a shared key names a shared player BUILD, so this is plausibly ONE unread build between five files and conversion, and it is the largest single detection gap named in this backlog. IT IS A LEAD, NOT A RESULT: nobody has read those players' bytes, and the idiom alone does not prove the engine. DONE WHEN the build is read and either a signature is added -- with a corpus byte-hash showing it moves ONLY files that previously refused, and docs/SURVEY.md's converting count rising by the number actually rescued -- or the files are shown not to be convertible with the reason written down. Do NOT widen an existing signature until the bytes have been read: this repo has a rule that a fix whose blast radius exceeds its evidence is scoped wrongly. ================ UPDATE AT bd28b6a: THE BUILD IS READ. The precondition this verify gates the implementation on is DONE, and none of it is to be re-derived. (1) `detect()` never throws on any of the six -- it finds the instrument table ($0BC6, stride 8, 27 records), the frequency table, `pulse_bounds`, `pitch_seq` and `effect_bit40`. The refusal is `convert.py:319 if not det.can_convert`, and the four missing fields are exactly `pattern_lo`, `pattern_hi`, `track_lo`, `track_hi`. All six share one build: init $100C, play $101A. (2) THE PATTERN TABLE IS INTERLEAVED at $1D50 -- `$1138 ASL A / TAY` then `$113A LDA $1D50,Y / STA $FA / LDA $1D51,Y / STA $FB`, so Y = 2 x pattern and the table is lo/hi PAIRS. That is `table_stride 2` on the PATTERN table, and no dialect here supports it -- every one assumes separate lo and hi tables. Its first pointers ($2010 $2013 $203E $204D ...) are ascending and land in plausible pattern data. (3) THE TRACK TABLE IS WRITTEN AT INIT. The runtime table the player reads ($1B3B/$1B3F, via `$1104 LDA $1B3B,X / STA $F8`) is ZERO-FILLED on disk. Init is `$100C JMP $18FF`, and $1919-$192A copies it: `LDA $1B43,X / STA $1B3B,Y / LDA $1B44,X / STA $1B3F,Y / INX INX / INY / CPY #$04 / BNE`. So the real table is **$1B43, interleaved, FOUR voices, 8 bytes per subtune** -- and `track_voices` is 3. (4) THE ANCHOR is `BD ?? ?? 99 ?? ?? BD ?? ?? 99 ?? ?? E8 E8 C8 C0 04 D0 ED`, which reads the source address out of the instruction that names it rather than off a fixed offset. Five files match at $1919 (src $1B43); Lakers_vs_Celtics matches the same shape at $1937 (src $1B6B), which is the 'one cell away' this task recorded. Subtune 0's four track pointers read out sane on all six. ================ AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT DETERMINES THE IMPLEMENTATION'S SHAPE. Corpus-wide that anchor matches **15 files, and NINE of them ALREADY CONVERT** (After_8, Kings_of_the_Beach_intro, Mr_Meaner, Off_the_Cuff, One_on_One_Jordan_vs_Bird, Powerplay_Hockey_USA_vs_USSR, Pygmies_Revenge, Rikky, Rock_Tells_the_Tale). So this MUST be a LAST-RESORT chain, consulted only where the existing track chain found nothing -- the rule `find_relocation`, `find_init_writes` and `INSTRUMENT_INDEX_SHAPE` already follow. A chain that sets track_lo/track_hi unconditionally would override nine working files, which is the blast-radius-exceeds-the-evidence failure this repo has a rule for. ================ THREE THINGS THE IMPLEMENTATION STILL NEEDS, none of which exists today, and they were opened as separate ids and folded back here because they are this task's steps rather than tasks of their own. (a) `nine-converting-files-share-the-init-copy-idiom`: the last-resort scoping above. (b) `the-pattern-table-can-be-interleaved-and-no-dialect-supports-stride-2`: pattern `table_stride 2` support, in `decode_entry`'s `step = i * det.table_stride` and wherever else the lo/hi pair is formed. (c) `a-four-voice-track-table-needs-a-fourth-voice-decision`: FIND OUT WHAT THE FOURTH TRACK DRIVES before emitting three of four. `CPY #$04` is unambiguous; emitting voices 0-2 and silently dropping track 3 would be a guess, and this repo's rule is that a guess about a player belongs in a measurement, not in an emitter. READ THE SOURCE TABLE ($1B43), not the init-written destination -- it is the only one with bytes in it. PROBES kept in C:/t, fv1_ prefixed; fv1_ptr.py is a reusable generic `LDA abs,X|Y / STA zp` pointer-table finder. ONE FIGURE TO GRADE: with DEFAULT options `convert()` refuses 15 of 95, where the preset-driven byte-hash refuses 12 of 95 -- different populations, not a discrepancy.

tasks.needs_main_reason: a corpus sweep or artefact regeneration outlives a delegated agent, and a fresh worktree lacks the gitignored python/tools/siddump-rt/siddump.exe -- without it the harness silently measures only the single-speed files
tasks.verify: **THE ATTRIBUTION IS DONE AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS REFUTED (v0.5.439).** Instruments 3 and 7 carry the five-step sweep (byte-identical programs at entries 15-19 and 44-48), 2 and 5 one attack byte each, and 11 none. **A NOTE-RELATIVE `set` CANNOT BE THE FIX**: instruments 2 and 3 are struck on exactly ONE note each (A-3 across 256 rows, C-4 across 366), so note-relativity yields exactly one pitch for them -- what we already emit -- and would move instrument 7's by up to 6 semitones against an original spread of 0.63. THE REAL MECHANISM IS A LINEAR FREQUENCY OFFSET: the original's within-cluster steps are the same ABSOLUTE +104 then +48 at bases 4112, 5392 and 8208, where a semitone shift would scale with the base. Ours sounds 5 pitches against the original's 16, one per cluster. tasks.title: Commando is the byte-exact fixture: may a pitch fix change it?
tasks.blocked_on: Commando.sng is the project's ONLY byte-exact fidelity anchor and 26 tests assert against it. Commando's voice 1 plays the wrong octave on 96 of its 237 voice-1 attacks (141 are already exact), and ANY fix necessarily changes Commando.sng and breaks those tests. THE QUESTION: may Commando.sng be re-cut when a fix is found -- and if so, against what (a new hand-verified reference, or simply the new output)? A 'no' is a good answer and closes the pitch task as won't-fix with a reason. ================ UPDATE AT bd28b6a: THE DIAGNOSIS IS COMPLETE, so this is now a clean yes/no rather than a question asked against an unknown. The mechanism is settled: note byte $68 = 104 overruns the player's 96-entry frequency table, and the player reads $54F8/$54F9 -- voices 0 and 1 STORED WAVEFORM bytes -- as the frequency. Instruments carrying $41 reduce to entry 71 and the one carrying $21 to entry 59, which is exactly the original's measured 95/1 split. We clamp every note byte >= 92 to GT_LASTNOTE (`patterns.py:495`), so voice 1 plays G#7 on 110 events. WHAT A FIX WOULD COST: reproducing the original means emitting a fixed very high pitch (entry 71 for a $41 instrument) rather than a clamp to 92 -- a 21-semitone move on 110 of voice 1's notes -- and Commando.sng is the project's ONLY byte-exact anchor, asserted by 26 tests. THE QUESTION IS UNCHANGED: may Commando.sng be re-cut and those tests re-based? Note the honest counter-argument, which did not exist before the diagnosis: what the original sounds there is not a musical note at all, it is whatever two waveform registers happen to hold, so 'faithful' and 'better' may not be the same answer here and a listen should probably decide it.

tasks.verify: THE DIAGNOSIS IS DONE AND IS IN bd28b6a; this is the emission question it leaves. `patterns.py:495-496` is `if g_note >= 0x5C: g_note = 0x5C`, so every note byte at or above 92 becomes GT_LASTNOTE. Commando's voice 1 carries note byte 104 on 110 events (plus 95 x8 and 93 x6, 124 clamped in total), and the player sounds those by reading $54F8/$54F9 -- voices 0 and 1 stored waveform bytes -- as a frequency, which for a $41 instrument reduces to table entry 71. GT's note column stops at index 92 and the player's table runs to 95, so SOMETHING must clamp; what is wrong is the VALUE. Three candidates and none is obviously right: emit entry 71 (right for the eight $41 instruments and wrong for the $21 one); emit per-instrument from the record's +2 byte (right per instrument, but the byte is voice 1's, not the sounding voice's, so it is right only when voice 1 holds what it usually holds); or keep the clamp on the ground that a 16 kHz register artefact is not music and G#7 is the closer listening match. closed.reason: ANSWERED, and the answer is that there is no mapping.
